chapter: Advice to youth and the art of drumming
title: Tiger Rag, getting hot and Kaiser Marshall
summary: Saunders explains the drummer's tricks on Tiger Rag in the late 1920s; DeMichael tells of Kaiser Marshall tossing sticks.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: But that was the thing, now, what they used to do. And the big thing back in the late '20s and early '30s was the Tiger Rag. That was a great tune. And then the drummer, he would have to see that the bass player would make that (sound) with his bass horn. They were doing the bass horns then. And then the drummer, if he didn't have the bass, then the drummer would take his snare drum off and blow into the snare side, (sound) and you'd get that sound from there.

And that was the sound from there, from the Tiger Rag. And then the drummer would get ready for his solo and he'd run all over the place and play on the tables and chairs and all. But this is -- they call that getting hot.
Well, I always delighted in the story of Kaiser Marshall --
-- that was with Henderson. They were playing a dance, and he tossed a stick up and never
bother about catching it. He'd pick up another one.
